title: In twin ECHAM5 AMIP ensembles, the July 2018 OI SST v2 step fully enters Southern Ocean air temperature (-0.34 K, 40-60S 0-120E) and removes its 2001-2020 warming; no remote response is detected
abstract: Question: earlier campaign work found a -0.28 to -0.34 K step in July 2018 at 40-60S, 0-120E in NOAA OI SST v2, the source of the CMIP6/CMIP7 AMIP boundary SST, and estimated its radiative effect with linear Green's functions. Does a full atmosphere model transfer the step into its simulated climate? Approach: NOAA PSL FACTS has two 25-member ECHAM5 AMIP ensembles (1900 to February 2021) that differ only in SST data (Hurrell merged HadISST1/OI v2 against ERSSTv5), and a 50-member ensemble with the Hurrell SST that we used as a same-forcing noise twin. We took the boundary SST from the model surface upward longwave flux and compared the July 2018 shift of the twin difference (32-month means) with shifts at 685 other split dates (1953-2015) and with the noise twin. Results: the model boundary SST shifts by -0.33 K (OI v2 minus ERSSTv5 in the data -0.34 K, AMIP 1.1.9 minus COBE-SST2 -0.27 K). Simulated near-surface air temperature follows one to one (-0.336 K, z = -4.6, larger than all other split dates; noise sd 0.008 K); the latent heat loss decreases by 1.7 W m-2 and the net surface flux increases by 1.8 W m-2 (not significant). The step removes almost all the simulated 2001-2020 air-temperature warming of the sector (+0.001 against +0.111 K per decade without the step) and 44% of that of the 40-60S band. The Southern Annular Mode index shifts by only -0.11 hPa (noise sd 0.37 hPa); no remote temperature, pressure or precipitation response is field-significant. The November 1981 HadISST1-to-OI v2 splice gives a transient -0.25 K cold period in the same sector (1982-1987). The ESRL-CAM5 FACTS ensemble also has the November 2021 OI v2 warm month (+0.14 K, 60S-60N ocean) in its forcing and air temperature. Limitations: one model for the twin test; the twin difference contains all ERSSTv5-OI v2 differences; runs end in February 2021; no top-of-atmosphere fluxes; remote effects smaller than about 0.7 hPa (SAM) cannot be excluded.
